intuition.title: Study context: Sol–gel rate and ordering
intuition.text: The authors connect acid-controlled silica condensation with film homogeneity. Extensive TEOS aging reduces ordering; BTEE aging has a weaker effect attributed to slower hydrolysis/condensation. This is source interpretation, not a quantitative rate model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Sol–gel and aging discussion

intuition.title: Study context: Two structural length scales
intuition.text: Fcc and Fm3m in the low-angle/TEM discussion concern the nanocrystal superlattice. The10.5/10.8nm values must not be used as atomic Au lattice constants. No atomic coordinates are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, XRD/TEM and orientation discussion

intuition.title: Study context: Micelle-mediated compatibility
intuition.text: The source attributes aqueous stability to n-DT/CTAB chain interdigitation and assembly to charge/hydrogen-bond interactions with hydrolyzed silica. These are authors’ mechanisms, not direct surface-coordinate measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Micelles and assembly interpretation

intuition.title: Study context: Unresolved variants
intuition.text: Two acid strengths are listed without sample assignment. BTEE has no separately stated charge. Representative optical/TEM/film-thickness observations remain separate from exact aging labels.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–5, Methods and figure captions

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Electron transfer from a reductant
general_background.summary: A reducing agent can supply electrons that change the oxidation state of a precursor. Coordination and competing reactions affect how that electron transfer contributes to particle formation.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Recent Advances in the Liquid-Phase Syntheses of Inorganic Nanoparticles

general_background.title: Ligands in solution and at surfaces
general_background.summary: Ligands can associate with dissolved species and particle surfaces, affecting their interactions with the surrounding liquid. A ligand shell compatible with the solvent can provide a barrier to close particle approach, helping a dispersion resist aggregation.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
